```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has a legally mandated demand trigger with named compliance dates: April 26, 2027 for entities of 50,000+ population and April 26, 2028 for smaller ones, sourced to ada.gov and the Federal Register. The extension weakens urgency but leaves 12–24 months of runway inside a 90-day sales window. B's demand is chronic pain with no forcing date.",
    "A's buyer universe is enumerable, and the micro-purchase threshold (~$10,000) lets a $29–149/mo product skip RFPs. That makes it realistic for one person to close a first sale without an enterprise sales team.",
    "A has a cheap, concentrated, sourced channel: municipal league booths at $1,300–$1,800 and sponsorships from $250. B's only direct channel figure ($87–200 CPL) is flagged as unverified and is high against a $29–49/mo price.",
    "A's core product (an axe-core scan plus a report) runs on commodity tooling and does not need ongoing 50-state data upkeep. B's stated differentiator, monitoring audit dates and rule changes across states, needs sustained regulatory-data work that the brief itself says a solo operator is unlikely to keep accurate.",
    "B's own demand evidence cuts against paying. The Reddit practitioners are handling the problem with spreadsheets, and the brief says the real competitor is spreadsheet inertia, not other paid tools.",
    "Both markets are crowded (A has 6–7 near-identical tools, B has 10–15), so crowding does not separate them. A's buyer is simply more reachable, and its trigger more concrete, within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's acquisition cost figures (Google Ads CPL of $87–200, CPC of $3.33–5.34) come from a source the brief itself describes as an AI-aggregated marketing blog, to be treated as directional and not verified. The affiliate figures are only an adjacent-market proxy (registered agents). So B has no reliable direct evidence of what it costs to acquire a paying customer.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has real weaknesses too. Neither brief shows that any competitor has paying customers. A has no CPC data, and one of its demand quotes is vendor marketing copy. The deadline extension may soften purchase urgency, and automated-only scanning carries a value ceiling and liability risk. A wins mainly on having a forcing function, a reachable no-RFP buyer, and a lighter data burden than B, not on proven willingness to pay."
}
```
